lead.title: Lampsy Health raises €1.1M to launch in Europe its bedside lamp that detects night-time epileptic seizures with no wearable sensor
lead.deck: Announced on November 27, the round for the Portuguese startup, spun out of Lisbon's Instituto Superior Técnico, is led by Fundação Ageas and Portugal Ventures, with Angels Way, Phira Ventures and strategic angels, on top of support from the EIC Pre-Accelerator. The lamp combines an infrared camera with an on-device AI algorithm that recognises the movements of tonic-clonic seizures (more than 97% accuracy claimed on over 9,200 hours of hospital data) and automatically alerts loved ones: already certified as a medical device in the EU, it targets a commercial launch in Q1 2027 in Europe and the UK, with a waiting list of more than 7,500 people across 20 countries.

milestone.title: London's Hammersmith Hospital implants the world's first patient with Restoria, Medtronic's new conduction system pacing pacemaker
milestone.summary: Performed the week before the November 27 announcement by Dr Daniel Keene's team (Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust), the procedure debuts Restoria CSP, one of five pacemakers in the Vitalis range that won CE marking in October. Instead of stimulating the right ventricular wall, it targets the heart's natural electrical pathways, includes a morphology monitor to track pacing over time, can be checked remotely and is more tolerant of radiotherapy.
milestone.why: Conduction system pacing (CSP) is moving from an expert technique performed with pacemakers designed for something else to a dedicated product from the market leader: a sign that the standard of care in cardiac pacing is shifting. For European rhythm-management startups (leads, leadless pacemakers, implant tools), this is the new clinical and commercial benchmark to reckon with.

brefsEurope.title: Cambridge forms spinout Pinnacle Neuroscience to commercialise eVRT, a 'headset' for at-home vertigo rehabilitation
brefsEurope.summary: Prof. Manohar Bance's team (SENSE Lab, University of Cambridge) has secured £248,783 from UKRI to prepare the device for manufacturing and certification, and £149,918 from the NIHR THRIVE programme to co-develop it with patients and clinicians, after £145,000 from Cambridge Enterprise. The ear-worn sensor checks that vestibular rehabilitation exercises are done correctly, and an app lets the physiotherapist adjust treatment; the spinout is being formed with Cambridge Enterprise and an at-home pilot is planned.

brefsEurope.title: Mölnlycke adds Börje Ekholm (ex-Ericsson) and Kristian Villumsen (ex-Coloplast) to its board ahead of its split into two companies
brefsEurope.summary: Announced on November 26, the two appointments are meant to support the planned separation of the Swedish wound-care and surgical products specialist into two stand-alone companies; Sharon James leaves the board. Bringing in a former Coloplast CEO, now chair of Demant, signals serious preparation for the split — and future portfolio moves in wound care.

brefsEurope.title: The European Commission publishes MDCG 2026-7 guidance on technical documentation assessment reports and PSURs in EUDAMED
brefsEurope.summary: Published on November 26, the guidance sets out how notified bodies file in the EU database their technical documentation assessment reports and their evaluation of periodic safety update reports (PSURs) under the MDR. It comes as the first four EUDAMED modules have been mandatory since May 28, 2026: dossier transparency is becoming an operational reality for manufacturers, startups included.

brefsIntl.title: Mediwhale wins its first 510(k) for Dr. Noon CVD, an AI that estimates cardiovascular risk from a retinal photo
brefsIntl.summary: Announced on November 27, the software combines a fundus image with age and sex to estimate the 10-year risk of a first atherosclerotic cardiovascular event and sorts patients into three categories. A direct comparable for 'oculomics', where several European teams are trying to turn the retina into a biomarker of overall health.

brefsIntl.title: Fudan and Huashan Hospital give voice to an ALS patient with a 512-channel wireless brain-computer interface
brefsIntl.summary: Reported on November 26, China's first trial of a wireless invasive BCI built for Chinese reaches over 95% accuracy at about 80 characters per minute with vocalised speech, and over 90% at about 110 characters per minute with silent speech, read out in the patient's cloned voice. The global race for communication implants is accelerating, outside the US too.

word.definition: Devices (camera, wristband or small EEG patch) that recognise on their own, through an algorithm, that an epileptic seizure is under way — especially convulsive night-time seizures — and immediately alert a relative or caregiver.

parts.label: Sensor
parts.role: infrared camera and microphone, wristband (motion, electrodermal activity) or EEG electrode

parts.label: Algorithm
parts.role: recognises a seizure's signature (movements, physiological or brain signals) while filtering out false alarms

parts.label: Alert
parts.role: notifies the caregiver or care team and time-stamps the event for the neurologist

how.t: The device records continuously without disturbing sleep: video and sound at Lampsy or Nelli, wrist motion and electrodermal response at Empatica, EEG signal on a patch at Epitel.
An algorithm, often on-device, compares the signal with seizure signatures, especially tonic-clonic ones; its performance is measured against video-EEG, the reference test.
When a seizure is likely, an alert goes to relatives or the care team, and the event log feeds the neurologist's treatment follow-up.

word.why: Night-time seizures often go unnoticed even though they are linked to the risk of sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP): overnight monitoring is an unmet need for families and hospitals alike. The category has taken regulatory shape — a 510(k) for Nelli (Neuro Event Labs) in 2025, Empatica's EpiMonitor cleared by the FDA and MDR-certified, Epitel's REMI platform — and the shift to contactless (camera) sensing opens up the home market. Lampsy's round shows that a certified, low-cost, consumer-facing device can raise early money with demand already visible.

startups.name: Lampsy Health
startups.use: Bedside lamp with an infrared camera and on-device AI that detects night-time tonic-clonic seizures and alerts relatives; certified as a medical device in the EU, raised €1.1M in November 2026 from Fundação Ageas and Portugal Ventures

startups.name: Neuro Event Labs
startups.use: Nelli, a seizure monitoring system that analyses audio and video with no body-worn sensor, FDA-cleared (510(k) K251506, November 2025) as an adjunct to monitoring in healthcare facilities; backed by the EIC Fund

startups.name: Empatica
startups.use: EpiMonitor, an EmbracePlus wristband + app pairing that detects generalised tonic-clonic seizures, FDA-cleared (K250515) for adults and children aged 6 and up and certified under the EU MDR

startups.name: Epitel
startups.use: REMI, disposable wireless EEG patches worn for up to 30 days, with the Vigilenz AI tool that flags electrographic seizures retrospectively; $26M Series B in 2026

sources.title: Lampsy Health raises €1.1M to shine a light on undetected night-time seizures
Only 27% of US hospitals can run an EEG. Epitel raised $26m for the rest
